recordedConditions.lateEvidence: Late results may be appended as late evidence but cannot silently reopen or mutate the closed revision.

recordedConditions.terminalOutcomes: Escalation cannot bounce among roles and terminates as resolved, rejected, split, blocked, or human-required.

evidenceCalibration.supports: The detector finds fifty-three low-confidence candidates using six alternating compressed producer-role turns: forty-four unresolved and nine with a completion signal.

requirements.requirement: The system SHALL NOT decompose or re-plan repeatedly without a convergence criterion, implementation milestone, blocker, or explicit stop.
requirements.adoptedRequirement: The system SHALL NOT decompose or re-plan repeatedly without a convergence criterion, implementation milestone, blocker, or explicit stop.

recordedConditions.revision: Every plan revision identifies its predecessor, accountable owner, triggering evidence, material delta, and affected causal-DAG nodes.
recordedConditions.convergence: Start with an explicit criterion such as decided architecture, executable slice, accepted decomposition, verified blocker, authorized deferral, or rejection.
recordedConditions.progress: Require a durable change in assumptions, decisions, dependencies, scope, acceptance criteria, or implementation sequence; restating or reformatting a plan is not progress.
recordedConditions.budget: Give each planning branch a finite policy budget for rounds, elapsed time, or cost; Phase 1A counts do not determine the values.

recordedConditions.implementationTransition: When prerequisites are satisfied, the next DAG edge leads to an executable milestone or explicit decision.
recordedConditions.reopening: New evidence may reopen planning through a linked revision without silently erasing prior decisions.
recordedConditions.scopeTraceability: Preserve parent and child scope and prevent fan-out controls from being evaded through task renaming.
recordedConditions.verification: Test legitimate refinement, unchanged restatement, new evidence, unresolved dependency, recursive planning, exhaustion, implementation handoff, and explicit reopening.

evidenceCalibration.supports: The detector finds thirty-six planning repetitions: thirty unresolved, five with completion, and one after completion; twenty-seven include a later milestone and six an explicit completion signal.
The threshold is repeated planning message type for one story, and no episode has a known likely cause; necessity, unchanged conditions, and harm are not established.

evidenceCalibration.receipt: Planning repetition evidence compared with approved DAG, retry, escalation, and implementation boundaries
evidenceCalibration.supports: Versioned deltas, finite budgets, convergence criteria, and executable transitions prevent planning from becoming an unbounded substitute for progress.

requirements.adoptedRequirement: The system SHALL NOT expand task fan-out or depth beyond policy budgets without explicit justification and approval.

recordedConditions.domainOperation: Expansion is an explicit idempotent domain operation and is not triggered by merely referencing another task ID.
recordedConditions.exceptionApproval: Beyond-budget expansion requires an authorized actor, justification, revised decomposition, impact estimate, and recorded approval before mutation.

recordedConditions.atomicity: Partial expansion failure cannot leave orphaned tasks or inconsistent parent state.
recordedConditions.identity: Stable task identity prevents evasion through renaming, closure, reopening, or duplicate delivery.
recordedConditions.joinPolicy: Parent completion deterministically requires every required child to be completed, waived, superseded, or otherwise resolved.
recordedConditions.verification: Test breadth, depth, concurrency, duplicate split requests, partial failure, denied and approved exceptions, renaming, reopening, and deterministic joins.

evidenceCalibration.supports: Seven low-confidence candidates meet the four-distinct-task-reference threshold: three potential explosion, three expansion with progress, and one unresolved; all seven have a later milestone.

evidenceCalibration.receipt: Expansion candidates compared with approved DAG, bounded planning, ownership, and deterministic completion requirements

requirements.requirement: The system SHALL NOT silently replace ownership through duplicate or repeated assignment; reassignment must be explicit, exclusive where required, and traceable.

recordedConditions.concurrency: Use compare-and-set semantics so stale and concurrent reassignments return explicit conflicts.
recordedConditions.roleResolution: A role-addressed request is not ownership until policy resolves it to an exact actor FQN and records acceptance.

requirements.requirement: The system SHALL NOT treat an execution-loop FINISHED status, successful shell exit, or model assertion as organizational task completion.

recordedConditions.stateSeparation: Maintain separate state machines for provider execution attempts and organizational work.
recordedConditions.evidenceTyping: Record FINISHED, tool exits, observations, artifacts, and model statements as typed evidence linked to ExecutionId and the relevant causal-DAG node.
recordedConditions.modelClaims: Treat model assertions as untrusted proposals until schema, authorization, causal, and policy validation succeeds.
recordedConditions.successMeaning: Successful process exit establishes only its own process contract, not correctness, completeness, acceptance, or mergeability.
recordedConditions.failureMeaning: Execution failure, timeout, and cancellation do not automatically fail organizational work; Tekroo policy chooses retry, block, escalation, or rejection.
recordedConditions.completionPolicy: Verify authorized actor, expected revision, deliverables, validation joins, blockers, and deterministic merge or release evidence where applicable.
recordedConditions.transition: Make completion idempotent, durable, and causally linked to the exact evidence set used.
recordedConditions.lateEvidence: Handle late or contradictory evidence through explicit invalidation, reopening, or correction without rewriting history.
recordedConditions.adapterRestriction: Provider adapters cannot write completed story or task state directly.
recordedConditions.verification: Test false model claims, successful but incorrect commands, provider FINISHED without deliverables, valid evidence, duplicates, stale execution fencing, late failures, and conflicting validators.

recordedConditions.ingressValidation: Validate every raw type against the versioned active message catalogue at ingress.
recordedConditions.rawPreservation: Preserve exact raw type spelling, payload, provenance, and source schema or protocol version in an explicit unknown or quarantine representation.
recordedConditions.effectRestriction: Undefined types cannot trigger canonical organizational transitions, routing side effects, or accepted facts unless an explicit active compatibility rule applies.
recordedConditions.aliasContract: Represent an alias as a versioned record naming source type, canonical target, effective scope or interval, schema transformation, semantic-equivalence evidence, confidence, approver, and rollback or sunset policy.
recordedConditions.confidence: Low-confidence alias candidates cannot normalize automatically; retain both the raw type and candidate status.
recordedConditions.failClosed: Schema mismatch, ambiguous or multiple targets, catalogue collisions, and attempts to alias an already canonical raw type return explicit failures.
recordedConditions.replay: A normalized view records the compatibility-mapping version and transformed payload digest and retains an immutable link to raw evidence for deterministic replay.
recordedConditions.history: Historical raw events are never mutated; they may be queried or deterministically reprocessed after formal catalogue or alias adjudication.
recordedConditions.deprecation: Deprecation and compatibility grace periods are explicit and versioned and do not authorize silent coercion.
recordedConditions.verification: Test unknown quarantine, exact raw preservation, prohibited organizational side effects, approved aliases, low-confidence non-mapping, schema mismatch, collisions, mapping-version replay, alias withdrawal, and later reprocessing.

requirements.requirement: Untrusted agent execution SHALL NOT run in an unisolated host workspace or bypass confirmation, security, resource, network, and secret controls.
requirements.observedBasis: Confirmation policies, analyzers, hooks, secret redaction, and container workspaces exist, but LocalWorkspace is not isolation, analyzers classify rather than hard-deny, and direct execute_tool bypasses loop checks.
requirements.adoptedRequirement: Untrusted agent execution SHALL NOT run in an unisolated host workspace or bypass confirmation, security, resource, network, and secret controls.

The local probe did not exercise untrusted production behavior. The requirement therefore adopts external, mandatory, fail-closed controls rather than treating provider safeguards as a complete security boundary.

recordedConditions.trustDefault: Treat model-originated execution as untrusted unless explicit auditable policy classifies a bounded workload otherwise.
recordedConditions.workspace: Run untrusted tasks in a uniformly pinned remote or container workspace; host LocalWorkspace is prohibited.
recordedConditions.filesystem: Use dedicated worktrees, allowlisted paths, explicit read-only and writable mounts, and containment against traversal and symlink escape.
recordedConditions.resources: Enforce network-egress, subprocess, CPU, memory, storage, elapsed-time, and concurrency policies outside the provider runtime.
recordedConditions.authorizationGateway: Route direct tool APIs, conversation tools, MCP tools, plugins, retries, and alternate invocation paths through one mandatory authorization gateway.
recordedConditions.confirmationMeaning: Confirmation means policy evaluation; deterministic policy may pre-authorize bounded low-risk operations without requiring manual approval for every call.
recordedConditions.analyzers: Treat security analyzers as evidence inputs rather than hard-deny enforcement unless a separate gate applies their result.
recordedConditions.secrets: Scope and redact secrets and release them only to the specifically authorized operation; keep control-plane credentials and organizational storage outside the sandbox.
recordedConditions.failure: Missing, unavailable, or failed controls fail closed and produce an observable terminal or escalated result.
recordedConditions.trustedException: A trusted local-development exception is explicit, time-bounded, isolated from production and historical data, and cannot silently become the deployment default.
recordedConditions.verification: Test path traversal, symlink escape, filesystem and network denial, process and resource exhaustion, secret leakage, alternate tool paths, stale execution fencing, and artifact export.

requirements.requirement: The system SHALL NOT assume cancellation rolls back external side effects; commands require idempotency keys and reconciliation after uncertainty.
requirements.observedBasis: Pause/interrupt cannot roll back external side effects already issued; reconciliation and idempotency are mandatory.
requirements.adoptedRequirement: The system SHALL NOT assume cancellation rolls back external side effects; commands require idempotency keys and reconciliation after uncertainty.
requirements.decisionRationale: Pinned OpenHands source establishes that pause and interrupt affect execution control but cannot reverse already issued external effects. Phase 1A did not test destructive production effects. The requirement adopts durable intent, stable idempotency, explicit uncertainty, and authoritative reconciliation without promising universal exactly-once execution.

recordedConditions.durableIntent: Persist side-effecting command intent and its idempotency key before dispatch.
recordedConditions.keySemantics: Retries of the same logical operation reuse the key; materially different intent receives a new key.
recordedConditions.propagation: Carry the idempotency key to the external system when supported.
recordedConditions.localLimit: Local deduplication may suppress duplicate dispatch but cannot prove whether an external system committed an uncertain operation.
recordedConditions.uncertainty: After timeout, cancellation, disconnect, crash, fallback, or ambiguous response, record the effect as UNKNOWN and reconcile against authoritative external state.
recordedConditions.retryGate: Prohibit automatic retry until reconciliation resolves the prior attempt or an explicit bounded policy authorizes continuation.
recordedConditions.cancellationStates: Track requested, acknowledged, execution stopped, external effects known or unknown, and reconciled separately; never report cancelled as rolled back.
recordedConditions.compensation: Represent compensation as a new authorized idempotent command with its own evidence, not a historical rewrite.
recordedConditions.lateResults: Correlate late results to the original attempt and prevent them from silently overriding a reconciled decision.
recordedConditions.riskControls: Apply stronger preconditions and approval policy to irreversible or high-risk operations.
recordedConditions.completion: Every asynchronous dispatch and reconciliation completes successfully or exceptionally under an explicit timeout.
recordedConditions.verification: Test cancellation before, during, and after dispatch; remote commit with lost acknowledgement; duplicate and concurrent retries; fallback; crash; late responses; unavailable remote idempotency; and failed compensation.

evidenceCalibration.supports: Pause or interrupt stops execution only at defined boundaries and does not roll back already issued external side effects.

requirements.adoptedRequirement: SMA lifecycle, contradiction, consolidation, vector retrieval, or training behavior SHALL NOT be treated as production-proven until an attributable end-to-end vertical slice populates and validates those states.

recordedConditions.attribution: Record exact source commit, build, configuration, model and prompt versions, input corpus, run identity, timestamps, and raw receipts for every qualification slice.

recordedConditions.unqualifiedState: A capability without passing attributable evidence remains experimental and cannot be represented as production-proven.
recordedConditions.training: Level 2 training remains deferred future work and is not required for initial v4 semantic-memory operation.
recordedConditions.authority: Passing a semantic-memory slice grants neither organizational process authority nor production-deployment approval; security, performance, recovery, and readiness gates remain separate.
recordedConditions.verification: Retain raw run receipts, expected and actual populations, quality metrics, provenance checks, recovery outcomes, and cross-store reconciliation for each qualified capability.

evidenceCalibration.supports: The frozen MongoDB snapshot contains 2,921 memory documents and zero interpretations, lifecycle transitions, canonical texts, embedding references, edges, retrieval events, consolidated memories, training candidates, raw artifacts, and themes.
Substantial source defines replay, lifecycle, contradiction, consolidation, vector, retrieval, and training-related structures.
Qdrant population, semantic quality, retrieval usefulness, successful replay, and the executable version responsible for each runtime memory are not established.

evidenceCalibration.receipt: Source/runtime gap compared with approved Step 4 SMA authority and qualification boundaries
evidenceCalibration.supports: Only attributable end-to-end execution plus semantic-quality and recovery evidence can qualify a particular SMA capability as production-proven.

requirements.requirement: The system SHALL NOT infer causality, handling, quality, or abandonment from timestamp order, intended recipients, message frequency, static vocabulary overlap, or snapshot non-completion alone.
requirements.observedBasis: TASKS 003–008 each record one or more of these inference limits.
requirements.adoptedRequirement: The system SHALL NOT infer causality, handling, quality, or abandonment from timestamp order, intended recipients, message frequency, static vocabulary overlap, or snapshot non-completion alone.
requirements.decisionRationale: The frozen event and workflow analyses explicitly separate presentation order from causality, intended routing from handling, frequency from quality, source presence from runtime attribution, and snapshot non-completion from abandonment. The requirement adopts those evidence limits as a durable epistemic boundary while permitting clearly labelled hypotheses and stronger conclusions when corroborating evidence exists.

recordedConditions.evidenceClasses: Preserve raw observed, normalized, computed or derived, inferred, and asserted evidence as distinct classes.
recordedConditions.derivedProvenance: Every derived or inferred claim records inputs, method and version, confidence, limitations, and raw receipts.
recordedConditions.causality: Timestamp or presentation order does not establish causality; require an explicit causal identifier or separately supported auditable adjudication.
recordedConditions.handling: Keep intended recipient, delivery, receipt, claim, handling, effect, acceptance, and ownership as distinct facts.
recordedConditions.frequency: Frequency establishes occurrence only and cannot alone establish validity, importance, quality, canonical status, progress, or harm.
recordedConditions.staticRuntime: Static source or vocabulary overlap establishes implementation presence, not runtime execution or historical responsibility.
recordedConditions.rightCensoring: Snapshot non-completion remains right-censored unless an explicit terminal, abandonment, cancellation, or supersession fact exists.
recordedConditions.quality: Role performance and work quality require direct outcome and validation evidence rather than message count, duration, or role label alone.
recordedConditions.joins: A referenced record without a performed source join remains REFERENCED_NOT_OBSERVED.
recordedConditions.decisionUse: Derived signals may nominate investigation or trigger review but cannot silently become canonical organizational facts.
recordedConditions.hypotheses: Clearly labelled hypotheses remain permitted and identify the evidence needed for confirmation or rejection.
recordedConditions.verification: Test shuffled timestamps, addressed-but-unhandled messages, duplicate frequency, dead or static code, absent joins, snapshot cutoff, and conflicting evidence.

evidenceCalibration.supports: TASK-003 included teams.messages only, performed no joins, distinguished intended recipients from evidenced handlers, and left historical catalogue intervals unknown.
Referenced-only nodes were retained without source resolution, timestamp order did not produce causal edges, and unsupported semantic relationships were not emitted.
Frequency and repetition were explicitly separated from quality, motive, root cause, and unchanged-condition claims.
No completion observed within the snapshot is one severity signal and not proof of abandonment.
Static vocabulary overlap cannot attribute historical execution, and static test presence is not historical passing-test evidence.
The weakest supported claim is binding unless corroborating evidence justifies a stronger one.
